name: Confirm Transaction
desc: Client confirms receipt of a S32PacketConfirmTransaction (server inventory transaction).

fields.name: uid
fields.desc: Transaction UID matching the server's confirm packet

writeup.p: C0F is the client's acknowledgement of a server transaction: windowId, action number (uid), and accepted boolean. It exists to keep container actions and the server's movement/state checks in sync. Because the server sends S32PacketConfirmTransaction after inventory actions and certain checks, the client's C0F echo is the server's clock for latency and state. That makes C0F the backbone of disablers (break the transaction stream), ping spoofers (delay the echo), and velocity filters (spoof the echo to desync the check).

processConfirmTransaction is tiny: it looks up the pending action number for the open window and only re-enables crafting if the uid matches and the window matches. Vanilla itself does not time out or penalize missing confirmations; the NetHandlerPlayClient normally echoes S32 back as C0F automatically. This leniency is what disablers exploit: cancel C0F and the server-side container logic stalls without kicking.

Every client in the corpus has a Disabler that cancels, delays, or forges C0F (Memeware, Nekoware, Rise 5.99, Rise 6.x suite, Sigma, Spicy, Tenacity). PingSpoof (Rise 5.99, Rise 6.x PingSpoofComponent) parks C0F together with C00 and releases them late. Velocity modules (Rise 5.99 Velocity, Rise 6.2.4 VulcanVelocity) cancel the S32 trigger and answer with a forged C0F so the server believes the transaction completed while the velocity was removed. Rise 6.2.4 Timer parks C0F on the ground to freeze watchdog's transaction clock, and NoVoid/AntiVoid modules cancel C0F while falling. The two new research clients add two more families. November Recode 2.0 mutates C0F on its EventPacket bus: DisablerModule rewrites the uid to Short.MAX_VALUE in its BLOCKS_MC mode, and VelocityModule cancels the C0F echo whose uid matches a cancelled velocity transaction under GRIM, or one C0F per hit under VULCAN. LiquidSense Dev parks C0F in queues (Disabler, PingSpoof), forges a C0F(0, -1, false) sentinel in the Tp and LastestHypixelFly enable sequences, and overwrites the vanilla S32 handler in MixinNetHandlerPlayClient so the echo always fires through the modified send path.

The accepted boolean and uid are forgeable. Memeware sends C0F(Integer.MIN_VALUE, Short.MAX_VALUE, true) to poison the server's transaction map; Spicy swaps the uid to desync; VulcanVelocity alternates uid 1/-1 to break Vulcan's velocity transaction tracking. The detection surface is the timing: a server that tracks C0F gaps (Verus, Watchdog) flags when the echo arrives outside the expected window, which is why disabler modes pair C0F with C00 delays and flush them together.

implementation.overview: The transaction echo that disablers live on. Cancel it to stall container logic, delay it to spoof ping, forge it to break velocity checks, or park it to freeze timer-based anti-cheats. Vanilla barely validates it, so the entire game is timing and uid correctness.
implementation.server_handling: processConfirmTransaction: look up the pending action for openContainer.windowId; if the uid matches and crafting was disabled, re-enable crafting. No timeout, no kick, no penalty for a missing or wrong C0F in vanilla. The client handler echoes S32 automatically, and modules hook PacketSendEvent to cancel or mutate that echo.
implementation.protocol_notes: Fields: windowId byte, actionNumber short, accepted boolean. Window 0 (inventory) transactions are sent frequently during normal play. The uid counter is per-container; S32PacketConfirmTransaction carries the same windowId/uid the server expects echoed. Clients that cancel C0F must still answer S32 for window clicks or the container desyncs.
implementation.anticheat_landscape: Verus and Watchdog use C0F (and C00) gaps as a latency reference for timer and fly checks. The Rise 6.x disabler suite (TransactionDisabler, DynamicPVPDisabler, Verus2Disabler, WatchdogDisabler, LunarDisabler, UniversoCraftDisabler, MMCReachDisabler, ExperimentalDisabler, TestDisabler, ConvertMovingPacketsDisabler) is one mode per AC family. The trade-off: forging uids breaks the container logic visibly (items snap back), delaying keeps containers working but is detectable as a constant lag offset.

modules.name: Disabler
modules.purpose: Cancel, delay, or forge C0F to break anti-cheat transaction-based checks.
modules.how_it_works: Mode-dependent. Memeware's Transaction/Latest Verus modes cancel C0F and periodically re-send forged ones (C0F(Integer.MIN_VALUE, Short.MAX_VALUE, true) for the autoban channel); Sigma's SagePvP/ColdNetwork modes cancel C0F when id==0 and accepted; Rise 5.99's Disabler has a dozen modes (vulcanCombat, ncp, verus, etc.) that cancel C0F in specific packet windows; Rise 6.x splits this into per-AC disabler modules; Tenacity AdvancedDisablerModule cancels C0F in specific states.
modules.vanilla_hook: EventPacket send/receive; event.setCancelled(true) on the C0F.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: Cancelling C0F for window 0 freezes the player's inventory transactions visibly; the modes pair it with C00 cancellation so the anti-cheat's latency reference is also broken. Verus-based modes in Rise 6.x (Verus2Disabler) also send C0B sneak/sprint to shape the state.
modules.variations: Memeware Disabler (forged uids, queue-based), Nekoware Disabler, Rise 5.99 Disabler (mode matrix), Rise 6.2.4/6.1.30 per-AC suite (TransactionDisabler, WatchdogDisabler, LunarDisabler, DynamicPVPDisabler, UniversoCraftDisabler, MMCReachDisabler, ExperimentalDisabler, TestDisabler, ConvertMovingPacketsDisabler), Spicy Disabler (C0F packet buffer), Tenacity DisablerModule/AdvancedDisablerModule. November Recode 2.0's DisablerModule adds a BLOCKS_MC mode that rewrites every C0F uid to Short.MAX_VALUE during the first 120 ticks after join, cancelling a single C06 as the second step of the same mode.

modules.name: PingSpoof
modules.purpose: Inflate measured ping by delaying the C0F (and C00) echo.
modules.how_it_works: Rise 6.2.4 PingSpoofComponent cancels C0F and C00 on the send event, parks them in a queue with a timestamp, and flushes them from PostMotionEvent once the delay elapses. The component API (spoof/blink) lets other modules request the delay for specific packet classes.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: Delaying C0F+C00 together keeps the two gaps consistent, which is the tell Verus uses to separate lag from spoofing. A constant delay shows as a fixed ping offset; varying it looks like jitter.
modules.variations: Rise 5.99 PingSpoof.java parks C0F+C00 in a ConcurrentHashMap with per-packet release times; Rise 6.1.30 uses the same component.

modules.name: Velocity (transaction spoof)
modules.purpose: Remove knockback while keeping the server's transaction bookkeeping consistent.
modules.how_it_works: Rise 6.2.4 VulcanVelocity cancels S32PacketConfirmTransaction when hurtTime == 10 (the knockback window) and answers with a forged C0F alternating uid 1/-1, so Vulcan's velocity check believes the transaction completed and the knockback was legitimately absent. Rise 5.99 Velocity cancels C0F/S32 pairs in its own modes.
modules.vanilla_hook: PacketReceiveEvent (S32 cancel), PacketUtil.send for the forged C0F.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: The alternating uid keeps the server's transaction map from desyncing while the velocity check is fooled. Wrong uid parity causes the inventory to lock and the AC to flag a transaction mismatch.
modules.variations: Rise 5.99 Velocity.java; Rise 6.1.30 VulcanVelocity.java; WatchdogVelocity/RedeskyVelocity in 6.2.4 use C0B sprint actions instead of C0F for their velocity modes.

modules.name: Timer (transaction parking)
modules.purpose: Freeze the server's transaction clock by parking S32/C0F on the ground so timer-speed movement is not caught.
modules.how_it_works: Rise 6.2.4 Timer, in watchdog mode, cancels S32PacketConfirmTransaction while on the ground and queues it for later replay, so the server's transaction-based timing reference lags behind the client's accelerated timer. Tenacity TimerModule imports C0F for the same purpose.
modules.vanilla_hook: PacketSendEvent (S32 park) + PacketReceiveEvent (velocity cancel); PacketUtil.TimedPacket queue.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: Watchdog measures timer via transaction gaps; parking S32 on the ground only works while the player is grounded, which is why the module cancels the park in the air. Tenacity's TimerModule references C0F only at import level in this corpus.
modules.variations: Tenacity 6.0 TimerModule.java imports C0FPacketConfirmTransaction; Rise 6.1.30 Timer not present in corpus, 6.2.4 Timer is the representative.

modules.name: NoVoid / AntiVoid
modules.purpose: Cancel C0F (and all non-movement packets) while falling into the void so the server never registers the fall.
modules.how_it_works: Rise 5.99 NoVoid cancels every packet except C03 and C0F while the player is falling below a threshold, keeping the movement stream alive but suppressing the confirmations and other state that would let the server finalize the death. Rise 6.2.4 BlinkAntiVoid/WatchdogAntiVoid buffer C0F with a blink component and release on ground contact.
modules.vanilla_hook: PacketSendEvent (cancel non-C03/C0F); motion check for the fall window.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: Cancelling packets while falling is a classic anti-void that flags on servers with fall-check timers; the packet blacklist (keep C03+C0F) is what keeps the connection alive long enough for the client to place a block or land.
modules.variations: Rise 6.2.4/6.1.30 BlinkAntiVoid and WatchdogAntiVoid implement the same idea with the blink queue instead of a whitelist.

modules.name: VelocityModule (GRIM / VULCAN transaction filter)
modules.purpose: Velocity cancel that keeps the transaction stream consistent: GRIM mode drops the S32 that follows a cancelled S12 and then cancels the matching outgoing C0F, so the server never sees the velocity transaction complete.
modules.how_it_works: On EventPacket.In, an S12 aimed at the player is cancelled (CANCEL, GRIM, VULCAN) or scaled (REDUCE, REVERSE); under GRIM the following S32PacketConfirmTransaction is cancelled too and its action number is queued. The EventPacket.Out handler then matches every outgoing C0F uid against that queue and cancels the echo when the uid was queued, so the transaction is consumed client-side. VULCAN mode instead cancels one C0F per velocity hit while the funny flag is set. WATCHDOG_SAFE cancels S12 and folds the vertical motion into motionY only while on the ground.
modules.vanilla_hook: EventPacket.In (S12 and S32), EventPacket.Out (C0F), EventUpdate (GRIM queue drain check).
modules.anti_cheat_notes: The uid-matched C0F cancel is precise: only the transaction tied to the removed velocity is dropped, so the container state stays in sync, which is the difference from blanket C0F cancellation.
modules.variations: November's approach mirrors Rise 6.2.4 VulcanVelocity (alternating uid spoof) but cancels the echo outright; the GRIM mode's transactionQueue is unique to this client in the corpus.

modules.name: Disabler (transaction buffer)
modules.purpose: Watchdog-style disabler that parks outgoing C0F and C00 packets in queues, then flushes C0F in small randomized batches so the server's transaction clock lags without the connection dying.
modules.how_it_works: The PacketEvent handler intercepts every C0F not already queued: when the uid digit count is 3 and the disabler is not yet armed it arms (abc = true), clears the queue, and starts the flush cycle; once armed it counts uid digits and, when fewer than 10 transactions have been flushed but the uid grew past 3 digits, flushes the whole queue early. Flushes release 3 to 9 random packets per cycle (or the full queue when the delay is even or divisible by 3 and the queue exceeds 100 entries) through NetworkManager.sendPacket. C00 keepalives get their own queue and are released on a separate timer, and every 155 ticks a C14 tab-complete with a huge random number is fired as a keepalive substitute.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: The uid-digit heuristic (3 digits arms, growth past 3 flushes early) is a fingerprint of this Watchdog bypass; the randomized batch size and the C14 spam are designed to make the gap pattern look like lag.
modules.variations: Unlike Memeware's forged-uid disabler and November's uid rewrite, LiquidSense's variant buffers real packets and replays them; the C00 and C0F dual queue mirrors the Rise PingSpoofComponent park pattern.

modules.name: PingSpoof (LiquidBounce)
modules.purpose: Inflate measured ping by parking C0F and C00 in a timestamped map and releasing them after a random delay.
modules.how_it_works: PacketEvent cancels any C0F or C00 while the player is alive and not already parked, storing release time = now + randomDelay(min, max). UpdateEvent with ignoreCondition (so it runs while the module is off) sweeps the map and re-queues entries whose timestamp passed via addToSendQueue. The min and max delay settings clamp each other on change.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: Releasing C0F and C00 together keeps the two gap series consistent, the same trade-off documented for Rise's PingSpoofComponent; the random per-packet delay makes the offset look like jitter.
modules.variations: The LiquidBounce classic module predates the Rise component approach: a HashMap keyed by packet identity plus a random delay, versus Rise's timed queue; the ignoreCondition update handler is the LiquidBounce idiom for running while disabled.

modules.name: Tp / LastestHypixelFly (transaction sentinel)
modules.purpose: Forge a C0F(0, -1, false) echo on enable as the first step of the Hypixel teleport and flight rigs, desynchronizing the server's transaction expectation before the C04 teleport hops.
modules.how_it_works: Both modules queue new C0FPacketConfirmTransaction(0, (short)(-1), false) through addToSendQueue immediately on enable, right before the C13 ability declaration and the two C04 position hops at y+0.17 and y+0.06. The forged uid -1 cannot match any pending server action, so the echo is silently dropped by the vanilla handler while the movement packets that follow do the real work.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: The uid -1 with accepted=false is a fingerprint shared by the AquaVit teleport family; it is harmless against vanilla (a wrong uid is ignored) and aimed at anti-cheat transaction tracking that expects a continuous echo stream.
modules.variations: Tp.java and LastestHypixelFly.java carry identical sentinels; TeleportCommand (the chat command twin) skips the C0F but spams C13 per path node instead, covered in the C13 writeup.

modules.name: MixinNetHandlerPlayClient (transaction echo)
modules.purpose: Overwrite the vanilla S32 handler so the C0F echo always runs on the client thread and goes through LiquidSense's modified send queue.
modules.how_it_works: The @Overwrite handleConfirmTransaction re-implements NetHandlerPlayClient's logic: resolve the container for window 0 or the open container, and when the server did not accept, queue C0F(windowId, actionNumber, true). Because the mixin replaces the vanilla method, the echo is emitted even when other event handlers cancel packets, keeping the inventory state machine alive. The same mixin forces the MC|Brand C17 on join and fires EntityMovementEvent from S14 handling, and its addToSendQueue injection raises PacketSenEvent for every outgoing packet.
modules.vanilla_hook: handleConfirmTransaction overwrite (S32PacketConfirmTransaction in), addToSendQueue injection (PacketSenEvent out).
modules.anti_cheat_notes: This is infrastructure, not an exploit: it guarantees transaction continuity so the disabler and ping-spoof entries above can park C0F without desyncing the inventory. The echo goes through addToSendQueue, so LiquidSense's PacketEvent sees it like any other send.
modules.variations: The @Overwrite approach differs from the eight classic clients, which leave the vanilla echo untouched and only hook the send event.

implementation.general_hooks: PacketSendEvent (cancel/mutate C0F), PacketReceiveEvent (S32 trigger), motion/tick events for release timing; Rise 6.x uses component-based parking (PingSpoofComponent, TransactionFixComponent).
implementation.client_variations: Classic clients cancel or mutate the live packet in the event (Memeware, Sigma, Spicy, Tenacity). Rise 5.99 uses PacketUtil.sendPacketWithoutEvent to replay forged C0F. Rise 6.x routes through PacketUtil.send/sendNoEvent and its PingSpoofComponent/TimedPacket queue; TransactionFixComponent (6.2.4/6.1.30) repairs transaction state under ViaVersion. November Recode 2.0 cancels or mutates C0F on EventPacket.Out (VelocityModule GRIM and VULCAN, DisablerModule BLOCKS_MC uid rewrite). LiquidSense Dev parks C0F in queues on PacketEvent and flushes through NetworkManager.sendPacket or addToSendQueue, forges sentinels in onEnable, and its MixinNetHandlerPlayClient overwrite re-emits the vanilla echo through the modified send path.

anticheat.overview: The transaction confirmation packet is the client's acknowledgement of a server transaction, and it gives anticheats a clean client-to-server round trip that is independent of the keepalive channel. That makes it the timing primitive for the timer and pingspoof check domains: Grim's Timer anchors the movement clock to the first confirmation after each movement, Frequency PingSpoofA compares the transaction ping against the keepalive ping, and classic timers (Azure, Negativity) use the same packet stream to discipline the movement rate.

checks.name: Timer (Grim)
checks.purpose: Ping-anchored timer check: the movement clock must never run ahead of the transaction round trip.
checks.how_it_works: A PrePredictionPacketReceiveListener. When a movement has been seen and the next WINDOW_CONFIRMATION (or PONG) arrives, it updates the known player clock from the movement clock. Each tick packet adds 50 ms to a real-time balance; when the balance overtakes System.nanoTime() the client is running faster than real time, the check flags, cancels the packet, and executes a setback. A clock-drift floor keeps the balance from falling behind the player's ping.
checks.detects: Timer cheats from about 1.01x upward, including clients that fake movement rate while keeping the transaction channel honest.
checks.variations: Grim's TickTimer, NegativeTimer and TimerLimit cover sub-1.0 and multi-account cases on the same transaction anchor; the comment block documents the transaction-gap proof behind the check.

checks.name: PingSpoofA (Frequency)
checks.purpose: Transaction-vs-keepalive ping comparison: a pingspoofer inflates the transaction ping, not the keepalive ping.
checks.how_it_works: On each flying packet it reads the transaction ping (measured from the transaction packets) and the keepalive ping. If the player has been online for more than 10 ticks and is not exempt (lagging, teleporting, TPS, chunk), a transaction ping that exceeds the keepalive ping by more than 50 ms fails the check.
checks.detects: Ping spoofers that hold transaction responses to fake a high ping for timer/velocity bypasses.
checks.variations: PingSpoofB in the same package and azure's PingSpoof check use the same two-channel comparison; Hydro's PingSpoof and Negativity's PingSpoofProtocol port it to their own ping trackers.

checks.name: Timer (Azure)
checks.purpose: Classic 1.8 flying-delay timer: the interval between movement packets must stay near 50 ms.
checks.how_it_works: On every PacketPlayInFlying it measures the delay from the previous packet. Intervals below 47 ms accumulate a threshold and compute the timer speed as 50 divided by the actual delay; after 7 consecutive fast intervals it raises a violation with the speed percentage. Intervals above 70 ms decay the threshold by 3, and a teleport resets it to -10.
checks.detects: Timer cheats that send movement packets faster than 20 per second, including timer variants in the 1.0-1.5x range.
checks.variations: TimerB in the same package adds a second timing axis; Frequency TimerA runs the deviation-and-allowance variant of the same idea on the flying stream.

checks.name: TimerProtocol (Negativity)
checks.purpose: Packet-budget timer: the number of movement packets per second must not exceed the server tick rate.
checks.how_it_works: On each packet-clear cycle it counts flying, position, look and position-look packets into a rolling per-second list, keeping the last 5 seconds. The mean and median of the counts are compared against the tick budget (20, or 40 in creative, plus a configured variation). An overflow of both mean and median alerts with a confidence derived from the player ping.
checks.detects: Timer cheats that exceed the movement packet budget per second, and packet-spam variants that inflate the movement stream.
checks.variations: CheaterDeleter's TimerCheck and PacketCountModuleManager enforce the same per-second budget on the Fabric packet stream; NCP's FlyingFrequency check is the classic ancestor.
